For spatial compensator design it is possible to use the classic principle of matching the signals, separated by some time period. In this paper the possibility of using multiplicative signal multiplexing on the outputs of single-unit compensator channels, realizing different spatial delay, is discussed.

articleTitle: A microstrip array fed by a non-homogeneous stripline feeding network
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of a new approach in the suppression of the parallel plate mode in striplines. A microstrip-to-stripline-to microstrip coupler was built and tested to illustrate the idea. Finally a sixteen-element microstrip array fed by this new type of feeding network was built and tested at C-band. The building of this array at C-band was a first step towards the application of this technology at higher frequencies, where the integration of the antenna with the rest of the system is required.

articleTitle: A far-infrared gas-discharge laser
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: One of the most expensive elements of the HCN laser is the resonator. The size of the laser is in principle determined by the size of the resonator. The resonator of the LF pumping laser used in medical studies includes a glass discharge tube with two soldered-in glass branch pipes with electrodes of excitation. Similar discharge tubes are used in lasers with direct current pumping. Using soldering when making the glass discharge tube is a shortcoming of these lasers since it raises a resonator cost and reduces its reliability because destruction of the discharge tube is most likely in places of soldering. Lasers with high frequency (HF) pumping need a more simple and reliable design of resonator. To eliminate the above-mentioned problems we used glass tubes without the branch pipes as a resonator.

articleTitle: Three-layered dielectric filling microstrip line filter for high-efficiency polyharmonic power amplifiers
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The design algorithm of a three-layered dielectric filled microstrip line (MSL) filter for high-efficiency polyharmonic power amplifiers is presented. In order to illustrate this technique, a 9-section harmonic filter with 40% suppression band was built.

articleTitle: Backscattering spectral and polarization features of the surface targets in centimeter and millimeter waves ranges
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this paper the results of studying the spectral and polarization characteristics. of the signals scattered from surface targets in the wave ranges 35, 4, 3, 0, 8 and 0.4 cm are presented. The mentioned signal parameters are connected with implementation of manoeuvring and vessel propulsion system operation (i.e. caused by vibrations and marine surface disturbance due to vessel motion).

articleTitle: Experimental research of interacting modes in a barrel-shaped open resonator
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The experimental research of the field and spectral characteristics of different types of oscillations in the barrel-shaped open resonator (BOR) in the 4 mm-wave range is undertaken. The interaction of TEM and TM modes under certain conditions is determined. The behavior of resonance curves and quality factor of the interacting modes is shown, while the distribution of electromagnetic energy inside the BOR is determined.

articleTitle: Specific features of surface electromagnetic wave propagation in a ferromagnetic semiconductor in the millimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: An external magnetic field significantly changes the properties of electric and magnetic subsystems of a solid body. The paper treats the structure consisting of a magnetic semiconductor with two types of carriers and a vacuum. Propagation of waves is characterized by a set of equations involving the Maxwell equations and material parameters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic properties of a periodic semiconductor-dielectric structure in a magnetic field
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The present work is aimed at investigating the zonal eigenmode spectrum in a boundless semiconductor-dielectric periodic structure. The configuration is considered in which the direction of periodicity coincides with that of the magnetic field vector (z-axis), and both are perpendicular to the layer surface (the xy-plane), while the wave propagates at an angle to the magnetic field. Compared with the above mentioned problems, the present method does not allow separation of field components in the Maxwell equations for the eigenmodes of the gyrotropic medium. The medium eigenmodes are elliptically polarized and each of them involves all six components of the electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: Influence of antenna pattern distortions on the quality of solar radio images obtained with the radiotelescope RT-2
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The influence of antenna pattern distortions of the radiotelescope on the quality of radio images of the Sun is analysed in this report. The mathematical simulation of effects of distortion is conducted and the valid asymmetry of a level of the first side lobes of the antenna pattern is defined. The model of the antenna pattern for the radiotelescope RT-2 is selected. This model was used in the procedure of image reconstruction.

articleTitle: Dielectric spectrometer for the liquids with strong absorption in the millimetre wave band
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The measurements of complex dielectric permittivity for liquid systems with large, medium and small losses in microwave diapason are carried out by waveguide and resonance methods. The test bench of reflecting type for measuring CDP in liquids with high absorption is presented.

articleTitle: Wide-band properties of metal-dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this paper, the operating bandwidth of a planar three-layered metal-dielectric waveguide (MDW) for single mode operation on orthogonally-polarized waves is calculated, depending on the geometry and material parameters of the MDW.

articleTitle: MM-wave amplifier on the basis of a finline - modeling and experimental research
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The results of modeling and experimental research of a low-power waveguide MM-wave amplifier based on finline are presented. The modeling was carried out with the help of a specialized interactive graphics system intended for the modeling of amplifiers of the given class. The difference between calculated and experimental data has not exceeded 10%.

articleTitle: Investigations of advanced coaxial gyrotrons at IAP RAS
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Main results of experimental testing of the 140 GHz/1.5 MW coaxial gyrotron (Russian version of the joint Russian-German coaxial gyrotron) are summarized. Highly selective properties of the coaxial cavities and a possibility to increase considerably the efficiency of a coaxial gyrotron by applying independently an appropriate voltage on its electrodes (without any design modification) have been confirmed. A successful use of the two-potential connection scheme for the frequency step tuning and output power modulation in a coaxial gyrotron have also been demonstrated.

articleTitle: A simple noise generation method for millimeter-wave therapy apparatus
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Millimeter wave therapy (MMWT) is now one of the recognized electric physical therapy methods. The great number of techniques available are distinguished from each other by various complex radiation parameters (frequency range, intensity, available frequency and/or peak modulation), and method of effect on a patient (duration of each influence and their amount in a course of treatment, the particular irradiated zones of a patients body, and effect to acupuncture locus) is known. That is why the spectral structure of a radiation is considered to be an important parameter. The variation of radiation spectra used in practice reaches from high coherent oscillations up to quasi noise and noise broadband (ten percent) signals. In recent years good therapeutic results of noise effects on organisms in all parts of the electromagnetic spectrum wavelengths has been proved by investigators in the field of experimental and clinical medicine. It is shown that the efficiency of treatment is higher than in case of quasi-harmonic effects.

articleTitle: Improvement in the immune system of farm animals in a contaminated (including radiation) environment
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Since Ukraine is characterized by a high level of the environmental industrial pollution and the internal and external radiation and accumulation of pesticides, nitrates and toxicants in the forages is a constantly acting factor, the present situation can actually be defined as an ecologically dangerous one. This results in reduced resistance of animals, and an increased number of illness cases already at the early stages of the ontogenesis (after that their genetic potential can not be realized till the end of their life even if properly treated). This is the reason that the development and wide implementation of accessible methods of immunity correction and stabilization of the animal resistance that will promote the realization of their genetic potential and increasing the amount of cattle-breeding product appear to be highly important. The most efficient and technological method of correcting the resistance in the present-day conditions of environmental pollution is implementing adaptogens as a fodder supplement. The authors have investigated the effect of preparations of the Echinacea purpurea on the productivity of different species of animals. It was determined that using the Echinacea purpurea enhances the sperm productivity of bulls by 28-44%, the egg-laying qualities of the hens by 15%, fertilization and hatching of chickens by 19%, number of young animals by 27%.

articleTitle: Restricting the computational domain in FDTD-modeling of three-dimensional problems with axial symmetry
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The paper considers the computation of non-stationary radiation in electrodynamic stuctures with circular symmetry using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. There is proposed a new kind of exactly absorbing boundary condition (ABC) at a spherical boundary which is usable in Cartesian coordinates. Realization and testing of this ABC were carried out in a problem of radiation of the axisymmetric pulse antenna fed by a coaxial cable.

articleTitle: Application of waveguide bends as electrically controlled resonance systems in mm-range
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Waveguide-ferrite (and as special case waveguide-dielectric) resonators are used in waveguide techniques of millimeter wavelength range as a selective frequency control system. Use of biorthogonality condition allowed one essentially to increase accuracy of calculations of such systems, simplifying the construction process of new microwave devices.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical band-rejection filters
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Band-rejection filters are used in microwave engineering to provide one or several suppressed frequency bands in the given wavelength range. For the mm and submm wavelength ranges this problem arises in the hot plasma diagnostics at experimental fusion machines. Here, it is necessary to receive a plasma cyclotron radiation signal in a wide frequency range, ensuring that no high-power radiation of microwave heating made by gyrotrons in a narrow band inside this range enters the receiver. Because of the wide application of quasi-optical equipment in plasma diagnostics, the problem of developing quasi-optical band rejection filters is timely.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of weakly relativistic large orbit gyrotron
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In recent years considerable interest and attention has been focused on the theoretically appealing possibilities of increasing further both the power level and maximum frequency of radiation using new schemes of interaction in a variety of gyro-devices. One promising class of such relatively new tubes is the large orbit gyrotron (LOG). Although its advantages for high harmonic operation are well known and theoretically proved not only for the relativistic range of beam energy most of the efforts so far have been concentrated on LOG with strongly relativistic electron beams. In this respect, it is of great practical importance to consider the possibilities for development of an effective compact LOG operating with relatively low energy beams. In this paper we present a conceptual design study of such a prospective device.

articleTitle: Multiplicative noise variance evaluation in mm-band radar images using myriad estimation
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In many cases it is required to evaluate the multiplicative noise relative variance in radar images, in particular, those formed by mm-band side looking aperture radars (SLARs). It is evident that. the more information about noise properties one has, the more effective the algorithms which can be designed for noise reduction in images. This evaluation, for example, is needed before image filtering by local statistical Lee or sigma filters or edge detection. These algorithms need for their normal operation the value of relative variance /spl sigma//sub /spl mu///sup 2/, which is not always known, and therefore, should be estimated. It is often desirable to perform this operation automatically. It is of great importance to derive an appropriate model describing the real-life situation for a certain application.

articleTitle: Application of the method of mm-wave dielectrometry for a study of molecular mechanisms of the microorganisms vital function
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The researches of molecular mechanisms of the vital function microorganisms are important for the study of key moments their cell regulation such as work of macromolecular complexes at transmembrane transfer of a signal and processes of growth. In the present work the method EHF-dielectrometry is applied for the analysis of molecular mechanisms of managing systems of E. coli cells. Water is one of the factors of regulation state of organism. Dielectrometry in the millimeter range of radiowaves allows one to carry out researches in conditions excluding updating and destruction of an alive cell on change of hydration environment parameters. This method fixes change of parameters of water components which has different connections with macromolecular structures of a cell.

articleTitle: Correction of experimental electrical characteristics of materials on the bounded frequency interval
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Submits the method of correction of the frequency dependence of the complex permittivity of some material on the bounded frequency interval participating in calculations of diffraction fields. We proceed from the assumption that one of components of the complex function is measured with a smaller error and consequently this component can be recognized as a "support" function.

articleTitle: mm-wave dielectrometry methods for prediction, prevention, diagnostics and individual treatment at acute cardiac infarction and cardiomyopathy
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The aim of this work is the elaboration of methodology for prediction, prevention, diagnostics and individual treatment of cardiovascular pathology relevant to the molecular-cellular mechanism disturbances of membrane receptors functioning in the adenylate cyclase system (ACS) and cytoskeleton complex. The authors use dielectrometry data in the region of free water dispersion in acute cardiac infarction (ACI) and cardiomyopathy. Dielectrometry at extremely high frequencies (EHF-dielectrometry) along with biochemical technology enables the authors to conduct cellular level screening when acting upon various control complexes of a cell with biologically active agents in real time, under conditions which avoid object destruction. For the analysis the authors use the modification of cell water environment conditions, resulting from component conformational transformations on the specific binding of biologically active substances. The integration of modern biochemical and radiophysical methods has allowed the development of a new methodological approach to the analysis of cell regulating systems using nondestructive monitoring conditions and operating in real time.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a system consisting of a grating and a layered chiral medium
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A rigorous solution method is given to the vector problem of electromagnetic wave diffraction by a system which consists of a periodic grating (which may be sufficiently complicated) and a layered structure involving a chiral medium layer. In view of circular polarization of chiral medium eigenwaves and due to the boundary conditions, the chiral medium binds both linear polarizations: E-polarization with E/spl par/OX and H-polarization with H/spl par/OX. On the one hand, this gives rise to new interesting effects, but on the other, this adds complexity to the problem and makes it a vector one.

articleTitle: Decomposition modeling algorithm of the Green's tensors for layered media and analysis of waveguide structures
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is a description of an algorithm and technique of modeling allowing one to replace complicated analytical accounts for calculation of Green's tensors for multilayered strip and slot waveguide designs by simple and evident procedure of construction of researched structure decomposition scheme and its subsequent analysis by methods of the theory of microwave circuits.

articleTitle: Frequency shifter based on the cross Doppler effect (relativistic frequency shifter)
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: We consider microwave frequency shifters based on the cross Doppler effect (CDE). We analyse the process of the change of the frequency of electromagnetic waves, falling on such a receiver, taking account of the quantum mechanical nature of the radiation. A circuit of the experimental installation for the measurement of CDE, which can be realized on the base of quasioptical engineering, is also presented.

articleTitle: Giant magnetoresistive effect in Fe/Cr multilayers in the millimeter wave band
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Transmission coefficient variations are observed in a Fe/Cr superlattice for millimeter-range electromagnetic waves. These variations are caused both the microwave giant magnetoresistive effect and the ferromagnetic resonance.

articleTitle: Millimeter magnetic spectroscopy of paramagnetic complexes Cr(V)
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The obtained results of the complex spectroscopic studies of static and dynamic characteristics of the EHBA(Cr/sup V/) and HMBA(Cr/sup V/) complexes diluted in propanediol show that the maximum polarization is achieved for the paramagnetic center concentration N=0.6/spl times/10/sup 20/ - 1.2/spl times/10/sup 20/ cm/sup -3/. It has been determined that the "dynamic cooling with the burnt out hole" is the dominating mechanism of dynamic nuclear polarisation (DNP) for both complexes. However, in contrast to the HMBA(Cr/sup V/) complex the effective diffusion of nuclear spin temperature is the distinctive feature of the nuclear spin kinetics in the EHBA(Cr/sup V/) complex caused by a different chemical structure of the used organic acid.

articleTitle: Waveguide filters for the microwave parametric amplifiers and convertors
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: With development of the short-wave part of the MM-range, special urgency is being placed on the search for new physical principles of designing frequency-selective devices with minimal losses and dimensions, high stability and reproducibility of the electrical characteristics. In this connection special interest is being shown in the frequency-selective properties of regular waveguides paths. In the present work the results of strict mathematical modeling and experimental research of rejection filters based on H-plane rectangular waveguide, are submitted. The high accuracy of implementation and manufacturing with a method using galvanic plastics provides a deviation of experimental dependences from the theoretical within the limits of 1 % and completely eliminates the necessity for experimental completion and adjustment of the filter.

articleTitle: Mixer conversion loss and receiver single-sideband noise temperature improvement by return of signal converted in image
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A rather simple and low cost method of improving mixer conversion loss and the single side-band noise temperature of a receiver was proposed and implemented. As a result the single side-band noise temperature of uncooled receivers was reduced to 770 K at a frequency 115.3 GHz and to 1500 K at a frequency 210.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave generation by relativistic electron bunches at the LINAC LIC
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Questions connected with the radiation of relativistic charged particles, particular electrons, are of significant interest for specialists both in relativistic electronics and in accelerator physics. The investigation of relativistic electron radiation allows one to obtain information about beam parameters, and the radiation nature (transition, synchrotron etc.) is of no principal importance. A beam at the exit of linear resonance electron accelerators is a train of dense bunches with their length being in the 0.1-10 mm range for most S-band accelerators. The number of electrons per bunch N is 10/sup 7/-10/sup 11/ . The radiation intensity is proportional to N/sup 2/ in case when the radiation wavelength more than a bunch length. The wavelength of coherent radiation of bunches is in millimeter and submillimeter ranges for modem linear electron accelerators. The aim of this present paper is the experimental study of coherent diffraction radiation from relativistic electron bunches accelerated in a linear resonance accelerator.

articleTitle: mm-band radar image filtering with texture information preservation
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Studies the texture preserving properties for different simple basic filters (of DPF and NSF types) in order to provide a possibility of using one of them in the filtering scheme for texture region processing. These properties have been analyzed both quantitatively and visually. The filters analyzed were the following: the noise suppressing filters (NSFs) - mean, median, and L/sub pq/ filters; the detail preserving filters (DPFs) - the standard sigma filter and the local statistical Lee filter.

articleTitle: Investigation of the atmospheric ozone conditions over the Black Sea region
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Black Sea and Caspian coasts are moderate to highly populated regions where many holiday and health resort installations exist. Ukraine and Turkey have well-developed infrastructure of oil industry, transport and refrigeration technologies. However, using rather old technologies due to historical reasons, manufacturing installations may release large quantities of stratospheric ozone-depleting substances such as CFC, VOC, NOx, HCF's, chloromethanes and especially of light hydrocarbons (CH/sub 4/ etc.) which is one of the possible sources that increases the O/sub 3/ concentration in the troposphere. Therefore, understanding and control of sources of pollution in the troposphere by O/sub 3/ and other stratospheric ozone-depleting substances is of great interest in this region. In this report we discuss preliminary results of joint investigation of the ozone layer over this region, on methods and duration of ozone observations and comparison of obtained results by satellite data.

articleTitle: The influence of microwave irradiation on human epithelial cells
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The authors studied changes in electronegativity (ENN) and cell membrane permeability under the influence of microwave radiation of wavelengths 8 and 16 mm. Experiments were performed on human buccal epithelium cells of four female donors of age 20-21 years. The data presented show the increase of stainability of cells after microwave irradiation and thereafter the increase of permeability of cell membranes. Almost the same increase in membrane permeability was detected after irradiation cells with microwaves of wavelength 16 mm. These phenomena are observed after 5 seconds of irradiation that is less than ENN reaction (mainly 15 seconds) and may be regarded as an evidence of cell damage.

articleTitle: On the scattering of electromagnetic waves by the infinite grating of thin dielectric strips
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The method of Riemann-Gilbert finds application in many problems of diffraction and propagation electromagnetic waves in the different periodic structures. It is a well-known fact that elements of periodic structures in this problem are assumed perfectly conducting and infinitively thin. This paper is an attempt to extend the method to the case of final thickness and final conductivity of the strips formed by the grating.

articleTitle: Frequency stabilization of IMPATT-diode oscillator by open resonator
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The suggested approach to the frequency stabilization by OR makes it promising for using InP Gunn diodes and IMPATT diodes at over 100 GHz. In order to prevent mode jumping and to ensure good matching it is advantageous to use the OR with additional restrictions of resonance space. Owing to the high Q -factor of the oscillating circuit, the frequency noise of IMPATT-diodes is reduced to the noise level of Gunn diodes. High long-term stability can be obtained by thermostabilization of the open resonance system.

articleTitle: Electron-hole processes in an anti-lock m-n contact
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The presence of inductive properties for contact of Sn-high resistance germanium of n-type has been shown experimentally. This is anti-closed m-n contact, which has /spl phi//sub m/</spl phi//sub n/, where /spl phi//sub m/ and /spl phi//sub n/ are the work functions of electron from metal m- and n-type semiconductor respectively. The inductive properties of anticlosed m-n contact cannot be explained in the framework of metal-semiconductor contact theory. Owing to it, the electron-hole processes into anti-closed m-n contact are investigated at applied direct voltage. The energy conditions of dynamic equilibrium for the space-charge region (SCR) of m-n contact, which describes the dependence of boundary magnitude upon applied voltage, are determined. The equation of volt-ampere characteristics is defined. It is shown that the differential capacitance of m-n contact is changing the sign from positive to negative under growth of reverse voltage, and is changing exponentially under growth of forward voltage.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave and radiofrequency absorption in melt-textured high-T/sub c/ YBaCuO superconductors
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The authors results show that, on the one hand, microwave and radiofrequency techniques can be important for quality characterization of the melt-texture HTS materials and, on the other hand, the latter themselves represent an interesting object for study of their high-frequency properties.

articleTitle: Amorphous microwires in microwave fields
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The results of ferromagnetic resonance measurements for microwires in the 75 GHz and 10 GHz frequency bands over a wide temperature range (300 K-0.5 K) are presented. Discussion and analysis of the magnetospectroscopy results are given in the paper. The possible reasons for the magnetoimpedance jump revealed in the vicinity of the low-field area are discussed. The disturbing influence of the microwire element on a high-quality open resonator structure is analyzed. We present here results of a thorough study of the resonance properties of microwires with the following compositions: Co/sub 68/Mn/sub 7/Si/sub 10/B/sub 15/; Fe/sub 69/Si/sub 16/B/sub 10/C/sub 5/; Co/sub 75/Si/sub 10/B/sub 15/.

articleTitle: The mode-matching technique as a basis of automatic solvers for complicated waveguide problems
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The main goal of realized project was to suggest a new generalized approach to mode-matching procedures both for calculation of sophisticated WG mode spectra and for calculation of the frequency response of complicated devices as well. Moreover, we have attempted to create fully automated algorithms that, permit one to avoid the stage of analytical consideration, i.e. to get rid of individual approach to each of the new configurations produced by practice. Together with special tools for recognizing the contours of WG cross-sections and their preliminary processing they provide the background for hookup to "mode-matching" solver - the comfortable interface for "geometrical specifying and editing". The classes of the objects that may be calculated by suggested approach include any WG devices with metal boundaries specified in Cartesian coordinate system or with the smooth boundaries that may be replaced by stair-case surface.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of electrostatic instabilities in magnetron diodes
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The electron dynamics in a crossed-field cylindrical diode are analysed by using a two-dimensional code based on particle-in-cell techniques. Depending on the prescribed emission surface current of the cathode, the numerical simulations reveal the existence of two types of regime in which the system can operate: an emission limited regime and a space-charge limited regime. In both types of regime, electrostatic modes are shown to be excited, the frequencies of which being of the same order of magnitude as the cyclotron frequency. The saturated states of these instabilities result in the persistence of large-amplitude coherent structures.

articleTitle: Coherent transition radiation from electron bunches in microwave range
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Describes the features of coherent transition radiation which is brought about by nonrelativistic prebunched beam. The beam strikes the finite metal plate or metal string. The experiments were performed in the frequency regions near 10 GHz. A bunched electron beam was produced by the toroidal cavity which receives energy from the magnetron. The receiver applied in this investigation is the outcome of an effort to provide a technique for measurement of the very weak radiation. The paper seeks to describe the principle of operation of this receiver.

articleTitle: Scattering of atmospheric millimeter wave radiation by spherical particles
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Scattering of microwave atmospheric and terrestrial surface radiation on dielectric particles suspended in the air can significantly modify atmosphere brightness temperature's angular distribution and cause some polarization effects. In this paper, radiative transfer calculations are used with a thin cloud model and a simple vertical thin cloud parallel to the surface, that is based on assumptions of spherical particle shape and homogeneous underlying surface. This simple model makes it possible to reveal interesting spectral and angular features caused by such phenomena and at the same time can be useful for description of microwave propagation under some realistic conditions.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous action of mm waves on the plant cells
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation of the radiofrequency waveband is the new antropogenic factor of the environment and research into its influence on the living organisms is of great interest. The radioprotective action of mm waves on plant cells, the embryo meristem of Hordeum L., Triticale-wittmarc, Secale L. and other sprouting seeds has been investigated. In compliance with literature data and the authors' results the mechanism of mm waves action and the formation of radioadaptive response have a complex character and is due to both the activation and the inhibition of gene expression, the functions of the energy provision systems of cell membranes, the processes of reparation and transcription, the regulation of events in the mitotic cycle. The reaction of plant cells depend on the genotype, the physiological state of subject, the time and condition after the irradiation.

articleTitle: Stochastic branching process model of phylogeny in mm wave range electromagnetic field
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Branching processes are used for models of phenomena in which something increases reproductively, for example the case of cancer biocells division. This kind of process can also serve as a model of other biological phenomena, that is, simply cell division (ontogeny for multicellular organisms), reproduction, and phylogeny. In other words this model describes life reproducing itself in nature. On the other hand, "scaling" is often observed in such biological phenomena. Therefore it is worthwhile to study what branching processes generate scaling and what physical mechanisms are at work in these processes. In this paper, we discuss branching processes of biosystems placed in an extremely high frequency (EHF) electromagnetic field (EMF) of mm-wave range (with carrier frequency of 60 GHz) as models of reproduction resulting in speciation, and as a model of phylogeny. In morphogenetic evolution (with the help of a morphogenetic field of electromagnetic nature and wavelength /spl lambda//spl ap/1 mm), the evolutionary process has long periods of stasis divided by periods of rapid change (bifurcations this pattern is called usually in the literature "punctuated equilibrium"). We compare this pattern with that generated by our model of the reproduction process.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Gaussian-beam diffraction on the impedance knife-edge using-the uniform asymptotic theory
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A Gaussian beam obliquely incident on the impedance knife-edge is considered here. The solution is obtained in the form of the Fourier integral. Some asymptotic simplifications for kr>>1 are deduced.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave quasi-optical power combiner
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The results of an experimental research of the power combiner based on the half-open resonator (HOR) are presented in this work. The HOR represents half of the usual spherical OR, which is cut by a conducting plane along OZ axis. Therefore, the modes are excited on this, which does not contradict boundary conditions on a conducting plane of the HOR.

articleTitle: Optimization of a horn-parabolic excitation unit of a planar dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Antennas built around the surface-to-space wave conversion have become firmly established as a particular class in antenna technology. They mainly consist of a dielectric waveguide, which forms a slow surface wave, and a diffraction grating, which serves to convert the surface wave into a space one. The variable coupling between the grating and the dielectric waveguide field determines the amplitude distribution in the antenna aperture along the surface wave propagation. Considering that the requirements upon width and sidelobe level of the antenna radiation pattern are usually made on both orthogonal planes, and that the amplitude distribution in the antenna aperture across the surface wave propagation direction is fully controlled by the amplitude distribution in the dielectric waveguide cross section, there is a need to resolve a further, no less important problem of forming a desired amplitude distribution in the dielectric waveguide. A new approach is suggested by the authors in which a special dielectric insertion is set in the open end of a standard flanged hollow metal waveguide as part of the exciter. Being a dielectric rod antenna bifurcated at the tip, the insertion improves greatly the illumination of the reflector sides.

articleTitle: Dimensional effect in the AC vortex response in thin superconducting films: exact solution in a weak DC magnetic field
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The surface impedance of thin superconducting films placed in a DC magnetic field was calculated by using a vortex dynamics model, which includes linear pinning restoring force (due to interaction with the film surface) and viscous drag force. Special account was made for dimensional effects in arrangement and AC dynamics of Abrikosov vortices, which are not considered in the well known Coffey-Clem and Brandt models. For the case of the DC magnetic field parallel to the film surface, the vortex ensemble inside the film exists in the form of separate vortex rows. The number of such rows changes discretely with the external DC magnetic field. The pinning constant (Labusch parameter) for vortex oscillations in the applied AC field is determined mainly by interaction of vortex rows with their images and strongly depends on the film thickness and on the magnetic field value. The "staircase" structure of the dependence of the surface impedance on the DC magnetic field is obtained. It corresponds to a discrete change of the number of the vortex rows inside the film. It was also shown that character of the dependence changes drastically with the frequency in the vicinity of the "depinning frequency".

articleTitle: New applications of superconducting linear and planar arrays of microstrip patch antennas
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The equations of planar microstrip antenna that represents the electromagnetic fields in the x and z direction as function of the electric field in the y direction are obtained applying the TTL method, at the first time. This method is very suitable at microwave and antenna applications, and gives accurate complex resonant frequency which contributes to obtain higher precision antenna parameters.

articleTitle: Parameters measurement of an anisotropic dielectric
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In recent years, great interest in development and use of radiophysical methods for determination of the dielectric parameters of materials has been demonstrated. In particular, characteristics not only of isotropic dielectric materials but also of anisotropic monocrystal samples may be studied using microwave methods (Sehlegeb and Stockhausen, 1972; Gilbert and Manfred, 1979). In this paper, a method of parameter determination for isotropic and anisotropic dielectrics has been proposed. The results of the permittivity measurement of a series of materials in centimeter and millimeter bands are presented.

articleTitle: 3-mm pulsed magnetrons for radar applications
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Millimeter wave radars have developed quickly during the last twenty years. They may be used as collision avoidance radars, for territory of air and sea ports observation, fire control, mapping, meteorological, missile-tracking, beam-rider, target-seeker and other uses. As a rule, such systems are required to have high accuracy and resolution as well as small weight and dimensions. In many cases to satisfy that requirement is possible by use of magnetrons as microwave generators. The problem is the strongly restricted choice of magnetrons in the short millimeter-wave band. Present report is a summary of work, performed in Institute of Radio Astronomy for creation of 3-mm magnetron series for radar application. During performance of this work the aim was to create a series at various powers, as possible low voltage, compact, and relatively low cost magnetrons having wide functional capabilities.

articleTitle: Complex dielectric permittivity of animals' organs and tissues. Measurements in microwave band for the needs of modern veterinary medicine
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The method of electromagnetic (EM) hyperthermia, being successfully applicable mainly in oncology and physiotherapy until now, has begun to be used in modern veterinary medicine for treating some widespread noncontagious diseases and suppressing the animals' reproductive functions. But for this it is necessary to have knowledge about the dielectric properties of the animals' tissues and organs in the frequency band 0.433-10 GHz. Because the data in the literature are not sufficient, in this work some of these dielectric properties were measured at 2.45 GHz frequency by the Wei-Sridhar technique. The technique's merits are its suitableness for in vitro and in vivo measurements in the whole coaxial line frequency band with good precision and simplicity. This method is based on measuring the complex reflection coefficients from four specimens: the sample under test and three for calibration. The measured tissue samples (muscle, fat) and animal organs (liver, kidney, spleen, brain, lung, testes, udder) were partially obtained from a Zooveterinary institute and partially were bought on the market. The measurements of the dielectric constants were carried out using fresh cuts.

articleTitle: Optimization of powerful relativistic Cherenkov oscillators
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Uses a general theory of interaction of a relativistic electron beam (REB) with a field of modes E/sub 01/ of an irregular waveguide. On the basis of this theory we obtain the one-dimensional self-consistent nonlinear equations of relativistic Cherenkov oscillators: reflecting travelling wave tubes (RTWT) and backward-wave oscillators (BWO). Then by partly optimizing parameters and profiles of regular or irregular corrugated waveguides the high-efficiency variants of oscillators are found.

articleTitle: Application of a specialized microwave source in biomagnetology
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The generator built was utilized for experimental researches on the influence of a low-energy electromagnetic field of EHF band on wheat seeds which were irradiated at a frequency of 38.05 GHz. The sowing qualities of the seeds were determined. The seeds of this culture were treated one day prior to sowing and were sown in allotments. The results of the carried out experiments are submitted here. The increase of germination was 8-11 %, the survival rate increased by 5-9 %, and the crop increased by 23-36 %.

articleTitle: Surface wave excitation technique for the 50-80 GHz frequency range near the low-temperature metal-dielectric interface
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: It is known that the basic directions of high-temperature superconductors for use in microwave techniques are the passive devices for cryogenic low-noise receiving systems and nonstationary Josephson effect based radiometry, fast frequency analysis and signal spectra and voltage standard creation. In these applications it is important to be able to synchronize the junctions to each other by mm-and submm radiation. It has been shown that Josephson junction array synchronization can be achieved by surface electromagnetic wave excitation near the spinal boundary boarder within a standard rectangular waveguide. Unfortunately, the sample size must exceed the wavelength significantly. We describe a superconducting surface wave resonator (SWR) for use in the synchronization of an array of Josephson junctions in the 9-34 GHz frequency range. The synchronization may be obtained by quasioptical techniques for the metal-dielectric. boundary especially for the mm-waveband. The purpose of this investigation is the creation of a surface wave excitation technique and SWR for studying in the 50-80 GHz range at low temperature level.

articleTitle: Coherent and incoherent backscattering of EM-waves by a semi-infinite random medium
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The equations for coherent and incoherent (diffuse) components of reflection matrix for a layer of disordered medium composed of chaotically oriented arbitrary scatterers, have been obtained. These equations are too complicated for numerical solution. We use these equations in a double-scattering approximation to consider the influence of particle properties on the opposition effects for semi-infinite medium.

articleTitle: Formulation of the power balance equation for a slot in a waveguide filled with a lossy dielectric
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Thin slots in waveguide walls are used as antenna radiators or coupling elements. Waveguide filling with dielectric provides miniaturisation of devices. All dielectrics are more or less lossy. The theory of thin slots in empty waveguides or ones, homogeneously filled with ideal dielectric, is elaborated quite fully. In this work an attempt was made to consider some questions of slot theory in the case when dielectric filling of waveguide has a complex permitivity.

articleTitle: Design and study of the high-efficiency diffraction radiation oscillator
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The main achievements in the development of the diffraction radiation oscillator (DRO) are brought together; the IRE NASU have created various DRO versions which at the accelerating voltage of 2.5 - 4.0 kV continuously span the whole mm wave region. With the feed under 500 W, the output power level varies from less than 1 W in the short-wave part of the mm wave region to tens of watts in the long-wave part. We seek to report the progress made during the last three years in further understanding DRO physics, in the extension of combined (mechanical and electronic) frequency tuning and in the enhancement of the DRO interaction efficiency.

articleTitle: Research of the noise spectra in the mm-wave electrovacuum devices
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In millimeter-wave backward-wave oscillators (BWO) and diffraction oscillators (DRO), the frequency instability near the carrier is stipulated by additive noise and modulation noises. In this paper, a model of the fluctuation spectrum of high-frequency oscillation BWOs and DROs near the carrier frequency was constructed. This model allows estimation of the qualitative influence of exterior additive and multiplicate noises on the oscillation frequency of resonant generators in the millimeter wave range and leads to extrapolation of experimental curves in a range of frequencies /spl omega//sub /spl alpha//<20 Hz. Further refining of the model together with experimental measurements of the natural and technical linewidth of oscillations of sectional generators will allow determination of fundamental flicker-noise components of the radiation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear theory of relativistic TWT with a slowing system in the form of arbitrary irregular waveguide
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: On the basis of general excitation equations for the longitudinally-irregular circular waveguide, the electrodynamic theory of the relativistic TWT with a longitudinally-irregular corrugated waveguide for the one-harmonic regime, have been formulated. This mathematical model allows the solution of the problem of optimization of the profile of the waveguide for reaching maximum efficiency of the E/sub 01/-mode TWT in the one-harmonic regime. However, because the nonlinearity of processes of interaction in the TWT and the formation of higher harmonies of the input signal (m/spl omega/)) in electron beam, E/sub 01/, and E/sub 0j/-modes may excite at m/spl omega/. This factor must be take into account in a more complete mathematical model of nonlinear processes of interaction in the TWT with an irregular slowing system. On the basis this model, the amplitude and phase-frequency performances of optimal variants of the relativistic TWT with regular or irregular electrodynamic system may be investigation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics of the microwave stimulated emission in dissipative paramagnetic systems
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Experimental, analytical and numerical investigations of nonlinear dynamics in dissipative paramagnetic systems (phasers and solid-state masers) under conditions of stimulated emission (SE) of millimeter-range electromagnetic and hypersonic fields were conducted. Due to the extremely low level of spontaneous emission in these systems (12-15 orders lower than in conventional lasers), it is possible to study such the systems as purely deterministic - in contradiction to optical range systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of scattered fields from an elliptic cylinder
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The work is aimed at experimental investigation of near field distribution of electromagnetic wave scattering from an elliptic dielectrical cylinder with different conducting strips on it and at determination of the distinctive features in their scattered fields.

articleTitle: Artificial millimeter-wave gyrotropic structure
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Summary form only given. A gyrotropic structure consisting of two gratings of wire helices embedded into a dielectric plate is proposed and investigated in the millimeter-wave band. This structure possesses the following characteristic property. At the operating frequency, the electric vector of the transmitted wave is rotated to an angle of 90/spl deg/ with respect to the electric vector of the incident wave, and this rotation angle is independent of the orientation of the latter vector. Based on this structure an isotropic millimeter-wave transmission polarization rotator is designed.

articleTitle: Novel superconducting switching device for microwave applications
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: We have developed a novel superconducting switch where the states of a quasiparticle tunnel junction (detector) are set with an external magnetic field generated by a control superconducting strip. Because the strip is only slightly overlaps the underlying junction, its non-uniform field with a high concentration near the edge strongly influences the junction current-voltage characteristics. A prototype of the device proposed has been realized on the base of thin Pb films separated by Sn oxide layers. A semiquantitative model of the switch operation using the critical-state approach is in good agreement with experimental data. After miniaturizing, applications in high-frequency superconducting microelectronics seem to be practically promising.

articleTitle: Damping of magnetic moment by swinging magnetic field in hard superconductors
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this contribution we report an investigation of the damping of the static magnetic moment M/sub z/ by a sweeping transverse magnetic field H/sub y/. We measure the dependence M/sub z/(H/sub y/) calculated under various conditions. All experimental results are discussed within the framework. of double critical-state and two-velocity hydrodynamic models.

articleTitle: Automation of the substance parameter measurements
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The appearance of power PCs on the Pentium CPU (or similar) base and improving program software, opens up a new possibilities in the magnetodielectric materials electrodynamic parameters measurement process in millimeter and submillimeter wave bands. Utilizing such a PC in the structure of automatic or semi-automatic measurement sets allows one to significantly expand the possibilities of similar measurement sets, increasing measurement accuracy and operation. Some results obtained during laboratory testing of semi-automatic set for dielectric material parameters measurement and control in millimeter wave band have been presented.

articleTitle: Radiowave control of media parameters from a flat interface
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Object of this work is the study of processes associated with electromagnetic interaction of a field of an open cylindrical slot-hole line (CSL) with a boundary layer of explored medium. The essence of the problem explored consists in existence of multiparameter dependence of a spatial, temperature and frequency variance of dielectric parameters of materials on density, moisture content and impurities.

articleTitle: Frequency stable oscillators based on cryogenic whispering gallery mode resonators
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: An all-cryogenic oscillator consisting of a frequency tunable sapphire resonator, a high temperature superconducting filter and a PHEMT amplifier was designed for the K-band frequency range and investigated. Sapphire whispering-gallery mode resonators possess high quality factors of about several millions due to the advantage of the strong electromagnetic field confinement. As a result the phase noise measured for the oscillator exhibits very low values in comparison to conventional oscillators. In addition, the effect of small rutile-platelets on the long-term temperature stability is measured and discussed. We have found that our composite resonators with rutile filling factor slightly below 1% exhibits a turning point in the temperature dependence of the resonance frequency at about 65-78 K. This results in a long time frequency stability as good as for oven controlled quartz oscillators by maintaining a high resonator quality factor in the 10/sup 7/ range at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Average power millimeter wave band travelling wave tube
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: There is a problem of development of TWTs with operation voltages in units of kV This paper presents the results of research and development of TWT on adjacent resonator chains (ARCs) for 8-mm and 5-mm waves ranges with output power of 5W and 2W, respectively. These TWT have 4-5 kV operation voltages. The 8-mm wave range TWT with much lower operation voltages of 2.0-2.5kV and output power of 2W is also described. In this device, as a slow-wave system, the double ladder structure (DLS) in the X-shaped waveguide is selected. To the authors, this waveguide type is the most eligible one for low-voltage TWT.

articleTitle: Microwave oscillator operating with the drift-orbital resonances in crossed fields
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A large-orbit side-cathode is considered for the microwave oscillator in this paper. A theoretical analysis is made of oscillator energy characteristics when shortening the operating wavelength. It is shown that this particular device offers considerable promise as a tool for the research and development work in short-wave band technology.

articleTitle: Optimization of an irregular coupled-cavity TWT
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The results of optimizations by efficiency of irregular usual and multisectional coupled-cavity TWT are presented. The efficiency more than 50% and power gain 30 db are indicated. It is shown, that using of subsections in irregular TWT allows to increase a band of gain up to 8%. The two-section hybrid device BWO-TWT with electronic efficiency 55% is discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of fractal conductive surfaces on parameters of transmission lines in MM-range
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The input in reviewing the a /spl alpha/-characteristics of components of an electromagnetic field allows one to apply adequate environmental models to the description of the processes taking place near to the conductive surfaces, technically defined as rough, porous, strongly cut up, etc. A lot of singular points (corners, breaks, edges, etc.), outlines or surfaces can be approximated by some fractal structure. For the description of fields near to conductors with fractal surface properties, the use of integro-differential techniques of fractional numeration is suggested. If it is assumed that the real structure of a conductor is approximated by a fractal ("thick") line, possessing by way of an expansion the properties of a line and surface, then the use of integro-differential techniques is necessary for the calculation of the field's /spl alpha/-characteristics.

articleTitle: Multimode directional filter for millimeter range receivers
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Summary form only given. In the development of high sensitivity mixer receivers within a broad tuning range, the problem occurs of supplying the local oscillator (LO) power to the mixer. The construction which allows the input both of the signal and LO power must provide their minimal losses because of the low LO power usually used. To suppress the LO noise, it is necessary to supply the LO power in the narrow frequency band which is formed by a high quality resonator. The multimode directional filter represents an improved solution to the problem of the LO injection to MM-wave receivers. The filter shows reasonably good electrical and mechanical performances in a 30% frequency band. The filter directional nature together with its resonant character provide both the low signal direct losses and the LO passage losses within the wide tuning range (85-115 GHz). The multimode resonator also gives a high signal-LO frequency separation. The filter was used as a diplexer in 3 mm range receivers.

articleTitle: Azimuth-homogeneous oscillations of a gyrotropic sphere in an external magnetic field
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Analytical and numerical research of azimuth-homogeneous monochromatic oscillations were made in a free gyrotropic sphere that was placed into external magnetic field. For azimuth-homogeneous oscillations all components of electromagnetic field are expressed through functions which are determined by solutions of the differential equations system.

articleTitle: Accurate technique for the 2D microwave dielectric-rod antenna simulation
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The effect of beam directivity improvement, due to an arbitrarily shaped dielectric cylinder taken as a 2-D model of a dielectric rod or lens antenna, is studied. The beam is simulated by the field of a Complex Source-Point (CSP) line current. An efficient algorithm for the solution of the 2D problem of wave scattering by a smooth dielectric cylinder with a "super-elliptic" cross-section that simulates a rectangle with rounded edges is developed, based on the concept of analytical regularization. The basic properties of the algorithm are studied. Numerical results for the accuracy of the algorithm and sample far-field radiation patterns for both E- and H-polarization cases are presented.

articleTitle: Micromachined low pass filters and coplanar waveguides for D-band frequencies based on HMDSN-membranes
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: This paper describes the fabrication and characterization of coplanar waveguides and low pass filters on thin dielectric membranes for D-band frequencies powered by transitions to rectangular waveguides. The membranes deposited from hexamethyldisilazane (HMDSN) were fabricated by removing the underlying silicon with micromachining techniques. Coplanar waveguides of various lengths based on these thin dielectric membranes have been fabricated and characterized as low-loss circuits for D-band frequencies. Two low pass filters with corner frequencies of 120 GHz and 170 GHz have been investigated, fabricated and characterized.

articleTitle: Characterization of the surface impedance of a superconducting thin film
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this paper,an algorithm suitable for the computer aided design (CAD) has been developed to estimate and model the main characteristic parameters of superconducting thin films. The detailed parameters of the superconducting thin film such that the surface impedance is described with the aid of the two-fluid model. An impedance function that varies with the temperature and frequency has been obtained. The attenuation constant has been computed and presented. The obtained results show that, within a certain range of temperature, the surface impedance exhibits negative real part. This negative resistance phenomenon is indicative of amplification which may occur if the superconducting thin film is embedded in a proper microwave circuit. It can be seen that the attenuation strongly depends on the frequency. The computer simulation results are verified by comparison with results using surface impedance formula of Mattis-Bardeen theory and show good agreement.

articleTitle: About normal clusters formation in high-T/sub c/ superconducting YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// films on sapphire substrates
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Measurement data of the surface resistance R/sub s/(T) temperature dependence of YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// epitaxial films on sapphire substrates are reported. The films were prepared by an impulse laser ablation technique. Surface impedance measurement was made in the 65 GHz frequency range. We shown that Rs(T) is in accordance with the epitaxial film considering the existence of spatial inhomogeneities as normal spherical domains. The analysis of YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// film contamination was made by a laser mass-spectrometry technique. It was shown that the normal spherical domains of the YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// films include oxidizer copper compounds filling cluster voids and film edges. The measurement was made for YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// films over the course of five-years.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of spectral interferometry method
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Systems using random signals, which have optimum function of uncertainty, provide a large signal to noise ratio, work in a continuous mode, with a low power, and allow one simultaneously to measure distance to reflecting object, and speed of its movement. For processing of random signals two basic methods are used: correlation and spectral. In the given work the results of an experimental research of possibilities of a spectral interferometry method (modified double spectral processing) are given which allows one to carry out distance measurements with high accuracy (within the limits of the certain interval), or absolute values of phase (difference of phases) of electromagnetic wave.

articleTitle: Linear theory of TWT in regime of radiation of electron beam flowing in metal-dielectric canal with diffraction grating
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The linear theory of TWT in regimes of Cherenkov and diffraction radiation of electron beam (EB) flowing in canal forming by surfaces of planar dielectric and diffraction grating is presented. The dispersion characteristics of electrodynamic system in EB radiation regime are determined.

articleTitle: Multiplication of frequency in the MM-wave range by using resonance-tunnel diodes
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The resonance-tunnel diode (RTD) is a high-frequency device and can operate on frequencies up to 1000 GHz. However, due to the RTD's capacity and double barrier, both quantum hole areas and contact resistance can essentially be reduced by the top frequencies of generation. The use of the RTD in the MM-wave range is possible by reducing the contact area (thus the useful scattered power and capacity of the diode decreases, but the useful power decreases to a level considerably smaller than that for Gunn and IMPATT-diodes) or by harmonic operation. In the latter case it is possible for either the generation of harmonics or the reception of harmonics as a result of multiplication. In the present work, the frequency multiplication by various RTDs is analyzed. The purpose of the work is to establish a definition of the frequency transformation factor (FTF) on harmonics.

articleTitle: Microstrip resonators with step and triangular discretization
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: This study describes microstrip resonators with step and triangular discretization which are a modification of the rectangular resonator. The study consists of analysis of a structure with two dielectric substrates and a rectangular patch which is varied in the number of steps in its width. This microstrip resonator is analyzed using the full wave efficient and concise transverse transmission line (TTL) method in the Fourier transformed domain (FTD) (Farias and Fernandes, 1997; Fernandes et al, 1998), in conjunction with the moment method. This study brings a singular contribution for microstrip resonators with new geometric forms, their respective peculiarities and analysis, through a full wave method. The results are good in comparison with other resonator results (Agrawal and Bhat, 1984; Fernandes et al, 1998; Silva and Fernandes, 2000).

articleTitle: Fluctuations of microwave emission of the atmosphere at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Spatial and temporal fluctuations of atmospheric emission at the millimeter wavelengths are caused by pulsations of the meteorological parameters such as thermodynamic temperature, liquid water content in clouds, humidity, phase structure and wind speed etc. These pulsations result from the turbulence in the troposphere. For a description of the fluctuating fields of temperature, density, humidity and, depending on them, the brightness temperature of the atmosphere, the authors use the so-called structural function.

articleTitle: Some results and prospects of the millimeter and submillimeter wave interstellar spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: It is well known that the millimeter and submillimeter part of the spectrum contains key information concerning the birth and death of stars and the evolution of galaxies. These are among the most fundamental problems in astrophysics. In. this wavelength region, one can probe deep into the cocoons of gas and dust surrounding stars in the earliest as well as the last phases of their life, into the dusty tori surrounding active galactic nuclei, and into high redshift galaxies undergoing their first burst of star formation. The radio astronomical groups from the Institute of Applied Physics RAS and Institute of Radio Astronomy NASU collaborate for many years in this area. Here we review the main results of our recent studies and outline the perspectives of this research.

articleTitle: Open resonator excited by a wave beam
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Open resonators are used in various millimeter, submillimeter and optical wavelength range devices: generators, wavemeters, filters, etc. The theory of resonators is usually formulated in the parabolic equation approximation. According to this theory a set of homogeneous integral equations is derived for fields on mirrors. Eigenfrequencies and quality factors of various modes are found by solving these equations. A research based on this method proves to be effective in the case of a quasiequidistant spectrum of the resonator using one of the indices, e.g., a longitudinal index for a two-mirror resonator. Dielectric bodies of even elementary shape, such as plates several wavelengths thick, placed inside a resonator result in nonequidistancy of its spectrum, the frequencies and losses of modes become dependent on the longitudinal index, i.e. dispersion introduced by the dielectric plate becomes essential. Methods employed to analysis of elementary resonators are inapplicable in this case. In the report the method of research of such systems is offered.

articleTitle: Nonlinear interaction of plasma polaritons in a semiconducting periodic medium
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The nonlinear interaction of electromagnetic waves in layered periodic structures is studied in the paper. We consider the two-dimensional layered structure that is periodic in one dimension and is derived by a recurring semiconductor layer and of a dielectric layer In consequence of homogeneity of the medium, the system of Maxwell's equations will be split into two independent polarizations.

articleTitle: Static electrical fields of reverse-biased GaAs- and Ge-pnipn structures
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
