abstract: The possibility of creating various semiconductor devices based on a reverse-biased semiconductor pnipn structure has been shown previously. It has been suggested that such a structure could be used for high energy particle detectors and chaotic generators. In these works the analysis of spatial-temporal dynamics of currents using the simplified model based on a phenomena approach was carried out. The modeling of the real physical process in a pnipn structure receiving external charge carriers (electrons) into a layer of multiplication of one of p-n junctions, was executed. However, previously the electrical field, which determines the shock ionization in p-n junctions and drift movement of charge carriers in i-region, was not strictly calculated. Therefore a problem in the creation of such devices remained open, as the geometrical parameters of the pnipn structure were not designed. In the present work an account of the electrical field is given and the parameters of GaAs- and Ge- pnipn structures are determined for p-n junctions of a particular geometry.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of CO molecule radiation at mm wavelengths in interstellar molecular clouds
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The processes of active star formation in interstellar molecular clouds lead molecules to a nonequilibrium distribution throughout the available energy levels. This is the reason why molecular clouds are sources of fairly intense radiation, with the frequency spectrum determined by vibratory-rotational levels of the energy structure of the molecules. It is known that in star formation regions molecules such as H/sub 2/O, OH, SiO and some others may be in an inversion state. Calculations have shown that under certain conditions in molecular clouds, the CO molecule inversion may also exist in the J=1-0 transition.

articleTitle: Whispering gallery mode dielectric resonators for the millimeter wave near field sensing applications
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The resonance characteristics of whispering gallery modes (WGMs) in parallel-plate type cylindrical dielectric resonators (DRs) are numerically considered to optimise their characteristics for sensing applications. Results for the dependency of the resonant frequency, Q-factor, slow-down factor and electric energy filling factor of the modes on resonator parameters for both isotropic and anisotropic DR are presented. The possible applications of the results for millimeter wave near field nondestructive measurements are discussed.

articleTitle: Computer modeling in the MM wave communication link design
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: We are looking at a rapid increase in the number of communication links and their transmission at higher and higher frequencies to answer the burst of information traffic. As a result of such activity, the problem of quick and qualified estimation of the real atmosphere influence on a link performance (possible attenuation as a first try) is springing up. Let us suppose that the link designer has the following problem: based on economical considerations or any others he must choose the antenna diameter, the transmitter power and the receiver sensitivity for both terminals and thereby determining the link budget where the atmospheric attenuation is included. This can be done using a computer especially when multi-beam antennae are involved. After that he needs the computer code, which permits him to calculate the attenuation probability distribution on the link located at in fixed area with a fixed frequency and elevation angle. Using this distribution one can find how much time in the year the link budget can be exceeded. If the received figure is unacceptable, the budget of the link under consideration must be changed and the calculations repeated. The computer code for the modeling is written in FORTRAN.

articleTitle: Thin-wire bolometer for measuring the focused laser radiation parameters
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A method for measuring the parameters of focused laser radiation using a scanning thin-wire bolometer with high optical resistance and spatial resolution is discussed. The bolometer withstands high radiation intensities and allows registering high-resolution profiles.

articleTitle: Optimum statistical filtration of errors in a complex navigational system for millimeter-wave range
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The proposed algorithm of filtration with requirements of a discrete character of operation of MMNS, allows one, by coprocessing output signals INS and MMNS in optimum fashion, to estimate coordinates of flight vehicle (FV) location, geographical path of FV, and error component of INS. It is possible to lower the requirements for sensing devices for an exact definition of navigational parameters.

articleTitle: Application of focused beams in millimeter wave super-near range technological radar
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: For a super-near range radar, distance to the object is comparable with dimensions of an antenna, which forms a focused beam. Such a beam effectively illuminates only a small area of the object and the beam structure is quite complex and different from the plane wave, when the RCS and radar equation are formulated. Therefore, it is necessary to obtain the functional, that provides the connection of radar parameters, measurement conditions, and received power - the analogue of the traditional radar equation for near field zone. Besides, it is important to study scattering characteristics of an objects observed in focused beams.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of a 2D parabolic microwave reflector antenna analyzed by the complex source-dual series approach
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The aim of our paper is to obtain reference data for the relatively large and realistic reflector antenna problems. Previously this has been done for the circular cylindrical reflector antennas, and here it is similarly obtained for the parabolic surface case. Directive feed pattern is modeled by using the complex source-point method. The problem is solved by the analytical regularization technique for the E-polarization case. Relative accuracy of the results and sample radiation patterns are presented in the figures.

articleTitle: "Quantum chaos " in 3D electromagnetic microwave system similar to Bunimovich billiard
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A 3D quasi-optical electromagnetic system with instability in the propagation of electromagnetic waves similar to the instability of a particle motion in a relevant Bunimovich billiard was studied. The purpose of the work was to find out whether can be implemented in the 3D electromagnetic system with a configuration of Bunimovich billiard a stochastic spectrum and whether there is a correspondence between properties of this spectrum and Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) spectrum.

articleTitle: A drastic facilitation of the onset of global chaos in periodically driven Hamiltonian systems possessing more than one separatrix
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Shows that there are certain frequencies of the driving force at which the overlap in energy between different-order resonances and the overlap in the phase space between the resonances of the same order are combined resulting in the onset of global chaos at unusually small amplitudes of the driving force. We demonstrate this in detail for a system with more than one separatrix, since the effect is most pronounced in such systems.

articleTitle: Installation of two-band radiometer at the BMSTU radiotelescope RT-7.5
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Until recently a one-band radiometer was exploited at the radio-telescope RT-7.5 for Sun observations. To receive more information about processes in the Sun in the course of the long-time program of Sun observations a two-band receiver was designed. By means of this receiver an intensity of radiation at the wavelengths 2.2 and 3.2 mm can be measured in every direction simultaneously that allows one to determine a spectral index. The receiver is assembled and installed at the antenna. Experimental operation of the receiver began. In accordance with the results some units of the receiver are being improved.

articleTitle: A new study of the transverse transmission line method in asymmetric unilateral fin line resonator
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The direct and concise Transverse Transmission Line (TTL) method is used to analyze unilateral fin-line resonators A slot resonator in unilateral fin line is a circuit element that is extensively used as a building block in the design of fin-line filters. In the direct TTL method, the Maxwell's equations in the Fourier transformed domain, are firstly used to obtain the electromagnetic fields in terms of the transversal electromagnetic fields. An inhomogeneous equations system is obtained, in which the current densities in the conductor fins are related to the electric fields in the slot. The TTL method in conjunction with the Galerkin's procedure and Parseval's relation are applied to obtaining a homogeneous equation system with two variables. The determinant of this system is the complex resonance frequency. The full wave TTL method gives precise and concise equations.

articleTitle: Polarizing reflection measuring set based on a strip metal-dielectric line
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Describes a polarizing measuring set that allows one to measure SWR (reflectivity's absolute value) and reflectivity's phase of the EHF band microwave devices, based on strip metal-dielectric line (SVDL), with adequate accuracy.

articleTitle: The method of analysis in vitro of molecular mechanisms of action of drugs for their designing, selection of doses and combinations
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The project objective is the creation of a new method of drug quality control and the express analysis of molecular mechanisms of drugs in vitro on the basis of dielectrometry in the region of free water relaxation. The methodology of the analysis was created on the basis of integration of the dielectrometry method in the region of free water relaxation, X-ray analysis and traditional biochemical technologies. It was tried out on bioobjects with different levels of organization, from macromolecules to cells. The studying by this method of the nearest hydrate environment of macromolecules with the help of the X-ray analysis has allowed the authors to construct the model of the hydrate environment. It was shown that the hydrate environment is a replica of the macromolecule structure and follows conformation modifications while its reorganization. This approach includes researches of biopolymer hydration, conformational modifications and reorientation of the biopolymer-water system under the structure functional reorganization of macromolecule and supramolecular organization.

articleTitle: Cylindrical E-wave scattering by a right angle dielectric wedge
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The solution presented in this paper, permits one to compute the scattered fields at any observation point. An asymptotic approximation of obtained solution gives both backscattered and forward scattered far-fields. A canonical method of field matching on the boundaries is used. Fields inside the wedge and outside of it are represented as plane-wave spectral representations in integral form in the right-angle coordinates. Then, the boundary conditions satisfaction leads to a set of IEs of the first kind for six spectral functions. These equations are solved in the class of continuous functions that is possible for a cylindrical incident wave. The Laplace transform of the obtained integral equations results in an ill-conditioned matrix equation (ME) obtained with the aid of quadratures. A new iterative scheme is presented for such equation solving.

articleTitle: Linear travelling wave array with two-channel excitation and nonparallel arrangement of subarrays
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In present work the results of investigations of linear travelling wave arrays with two-channel excitation for a case of a non-parallel arrangement of their parts are presented and the comparison of the characteristics of various types of the arrays with two-channel excitation is carried out.

articleTitle: A full wave analysis of metal strip on thin film semiconductor and its interaction with surface acoustic wave using moment method technique
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The moment method technique is formulated to carry out a full wave analysis of a periodic metal strip on thin film semiconductor. A number of basis and testing functions which verify the boundary conditions of electric field are assumed for the solution. The solution gives electric field distribution as well as potential and charge distribution. The surface impedance can be calculated using the relation of potential and charge density. The impedance calculations lead to application in transmission line structure as well as interaction with surface acoustic wave. The influence of surface impedance on the propagation characteristics of surface acoustic waves is presented. A small number of basis functions which reduce computational time give good results. Our results agree very well with data of Green's function.

articleTitle: The phase locked loop as a detector of the resonance absorption in gases [ESR spectrometers]
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Attempts to construct the spectrometer with autodyne reception on the basis of commercial BWOs. The main differences of the proposed structure of the spectrometer from the usual absorption device are: the strong coupling between radiation source (BWO) and absorbing cell is provided; the detector at the output side of the absorbing cell is replaced by a mirror (adjustable short); the information about the gas absorption (real and imaginary parts of the susceptibility of the investigated gas) is obtained from the output of the phase locked loop (PLL) of the backward wave oscillator (BWO).

articleTitle: Q-factors of a waveguide dielectric resonator with two-layer dielectric on the H/sub on/spl delta// modes oscillations types
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Waveguide-dielectric resonators (WDR) are widely used to create active and passive components and devices in the microwave band. The resonance properties of the WDR with a two-layer dielectric element (DE) have been investigated previously. This paper is devoted to the study of the unloaded and partial Q-factors of the resonator built around an evanescent circular waveguide for the axial-symmetrical H/sub on/spl delta// oscillation types.

articleTitle: Spectral features of the spiky sea backscattering at grazing angles
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The results of experimental investigation of signal spectral characteristics for millimeter band of radiowaves (frequency band from 10 to 140 GHz) are presented for situations when signals are scattered by the sea surface at grazing angles. The specific feature of the presented material is the special attention to two states of nonstationary scattering: a) signal intensity spikes caused by sea wave breaking and b) pauses when this effect is absent. From the point of view of data statistical processing this phenomena is connected with the necessity of process analysis for short time intervals during which processes can be considered as stationary.

articleTitle: Simulation of electromagnetic radiations by different human organs
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The human organism is a dynamic automatically adjusting structure. Its stability is provided by the continuous operation of different physiological systems. The variation of physiological parameters of an organism results in changes of the physical properties of biological tissues: temperatures, dielectric constant, magnetic permeability, electrical impedance, potentials, currents etc. One of the most effective methods of human organism studying is the receiving of continuous information on the indicated characteristics. Now this problem has been successfully solved with the help of radiometers based on radiophysical research techniques for studying of the electromagnetic fields radiated and dissipated by human organism. The results of experimental researches have shown that radiothermometry in the indicated wave bands, contrary to infra-red thermal imaging, shows information on dynamic temperature changes in more significant skin depth in real time, and the effect of thermal protection and thermal stabilizing operation of surface layers of skin on the observed data of temperatures inside the object is reduced. The quality of the radiobrightness map is influenced weakly by keratosic layers of false skin, hair cover, and thin clothes. The obtained data testify that panoramic and detail thermography can become rather useful in surgery, traumatology, intensive care, physiotherapy and other fields of medicine.

articleTitle: Comparison of the FDTD and direct-integrating algorithms for solution of the one-dimensional nonstationary electrodynamic problem
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Electromagnetic propagation in media with time-varying parameters is of interest for many applications: shock waves, strong laser fields, nuclear burst, atmospheric or environmental change and others. As a rule, an exact consideration of electromagnetic processes in media with the time-varying parameters is possible in special cases only. In the general case, an initial electromagnetic problem can be investigated by numerical methods. FDTD methods are popular due to their clarity and elegant realization in numerical algorithms. The integral equations approach seems to have a more promising future in terms of both reflection-free realization and stability. An advantage of the integral equation method is that it can be generalized to nonlinear dispersive materials. In this paper both FDTD and the integral equation approaches are investigated, accuracy and stability comparison of these methods are examined. Special computer modeling software is developed for dispatching the numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Nonlinear surface polaritons in 2D electron system
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Surface polaritons (SP) in nonlinear media possess some new unusual features in comparison with SP in linear media. For example, an excitation of SP becomes possible without using prisms and periodical structures. It can occur when a finite wave train falls directly upon the interface.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave oscillator based dielectric hemisphere with cylinder shield
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is the investigation of the main Gunn diode oscillator characteristics with a hemispherical dielectric resonator which is shielded by a metal cylinder. The frequency, output power and electronic tuning of frequency, the steepness of which allows one to estimate the frequency stability in relation to the parasitic change of the Gunn diode voltage, and their comparative analysis with the characteristics of generation in a similar open dielectric resonator.

articleTitle: Transmission matrix of the axial symmetric resonator with piece-homogeneous metal dielectric filling
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Addition of a grating consisting of perfectly conducting and infinitely thin rings in the axial symmetric resonator stabilises its spectrum characteristics, increases the Q-factor of the oscillations and the gradient of the dependencies of natural frequencies on the material parameters of the filling, and allows one to model the system without mechanical control. The dispersion and amplitude-frequency properties of the axial symmetric resonator with piece-homogeneous filling and the frequent periodic grating of varying radius are analysed in this paper.

articleTitle: Influence of the secondary electrons on the space charge oscillations in the gyrotron adiabatic trap
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: One of the characteristic features of magnetron injection guns (MIGs) forming intense helical electron beams (HEB) is the trapped magnetic field distribution and, therefore, some of the electrons with the greatest oscillatory velocities are reflected from the magnetic mirror, becoming locked into the adiabatic trap between the cathode and cavity. The trapped electrons (TE) degrade the helical electron beam quality and can initiate beam instability in some regimes. In this work the influence of TE on the beam parameters is considered. The numerical simulation of HEBs was carried out on the basis of the PIC-method within the quasi-static model of the electric field. The self-consistent beam magnetic field was not taken into account. The numerical simulation was carried out taking into account the initial azimuthal velocity spread on the cathode, which allows one to consider the joint action of the emitting surface roughness and the thermal velocities of the electrons.

articleTitle: Usage of millimeter waves in an on-board radar for detection of objects at small depth in ground
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The principle of construction of millimeter-wave radar for detection of objects at small depth in ground from a flying vehicle is offered. In millimeter wavelength range it is possible to generate a sounding signal of very short duration (1 ns or less), which ensures a necessary resolution of depth. Other advantages of millimeter wavelength range is, that it allows one to ensure a high directivity of an airborne antenna at the acceptable dimensions of an antenna and to decrease the square of the irradiated section of the Earth's surface. It essentially diminishes temporal extent of passive background interference from the Earth's surface and allows detection of underground objects at small depth in the ground. However in a given set of cases it is not enough, as the Earth's surface is irradiated with side lobes of an airborne antenna, to lower which below -20 dB by known means is usually very difficult. Therefore selection of a weak echo signal returned from an underground object at small depth in ground out of intensive passive background interference of the Earth's surface requires application of special hardware. The essence of signal processing and its technical realization is illustrated.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave investigations of the vertical ozone distribution over Moscow
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The presented results of ground-based millimeter (MM) wave measurements of the vertical ozone distribution over the Lebedev Physical Institute in Moscow are consistent with the general picture of global changes in the ozonosphere. High accuracy and reliability of the method, its low weather dependence and possibility of day-and-night measurements allow MM-wave spectrometers to be used for long-term, continuous monitoring of the ozone layer and detection of its depletion. Both dynamical and photochemical processes in middle atmosphere may be studied through ozone measurements at MM waves. The investigations should be continued for better understanding the phenomena observed. Additionally, simultaneous measurements of ozone destroying ClO molecules at 204 GHz are planned in future.

articleTitle: Mm-wave dielectrometry methods for express-control of intensity development and physiological state of algae
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: For studying phytoplankton, and also in the cultivation of microscopic algae in culture and industrial production, the regular control of intensity development and physiological state of organisms is indispensable. Conventional microscopic, spectrophotometric and weight methods of the registration of quantitative metrics are durable enough. In this connection of considerable concern is the development of new methods of measurement of the parameters of native cells (for example, differential fluorimetry, hydration degree of cells and state of cells water) which enable one to overcome these difficulties and to receive the new information. In this work the authors carried out analyses of the usage of modern biophysical methods - fluorometry and dielectrometry in the region of free water dispersion of suspensions of native cells for an estimation of intensity of increase of a biomass of microalgas. Both methods, fluorometry and EHF-dielectrometry, have major advantages - they enable one to work with the nonbroken frame of a living cell.

articleTitle: Research of a functional status adrenoreceptor complexes platelet of the hypertensive patients in the physical stress modelling
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Changes of platelet function play a crucial role in the development of tromogenic complications in hypertension and require correction from early stages of the disease. Special load tests provide the possibility to reveal the latent disturbances of the adrenergic activity and the platelet functional state. The aim of this study was to estimate the disorders of adrenoreceptor activity in hypertensive patients resulting from an exercise test. It is concluded that in the hypertensive patients an increase of adrenoreception and functional platelet activity were revealed. At the early stage of disease the physical load stimulates the trigger mechanisms of biochemical intracellular reactions which causes the altered platelet adrenaline response.

articleTitle: Atomic functions and direct methods for solving singular integral equations of electromagnetics
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Atomic functions (AF) are compactly supported infinitely differentiable solutions of functional differential equations, e.g. linear with constant coefficients and linear transformations of an independent variable. In this paper we propose a new numerical technique for solving boundary value problems of electromagnetics. As is known, these problems can be reduced to solving singular integral equations (SIE). For their numerical realization some approximate methods are applicable. We propose a new approach for numerical solving SIE based on AF. Some theoretical questions of existence, uniqueness, and accuracy of an approximate solution are considered. Approximation and computational properties of AF allow us to improve essentially the procedure of SIE evaluation.

articleTitle: Modulator of polarization for a quasioptical transmission line
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: This work deals with the new method of polarization transformation and control for the electromagnetic waves. Also a design of modulator of polarization for the quasioptical transmission line, operating in the range of millimeter and submillimeter waves is presented. Some particularities of modulator opermodulaation are described as well as the experiments provided. Our primary aim was to develop and create a simple, reliable and high-speed modulator of polarization of electromagnetic wave operating in a wide frequency band, capable both to convert and to encode the polarization of a wave. Suitable devices for this purpose found in millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths range were that of 20 mm diameter hollow dielectric waveguide-based quasioptical transmission line devices designed at the IRE NAS of Ukraine.

articleTitle: Influence of polymorphism of acentric ferroelastic solid-state structures on the propagation of sub-mm waves
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Ferroelastic solid-state structures belong to the most perspective materials of SubMM electronics. The exclusive position of these materials is determined by three circumstances. First, behaviour of ferroelastic solid-state structures in the SubMM wave range is not determined by a response of an electronic subsystem. The interaction of the SubMM wave with the solid is determined by an ionic bulk of the crystal lattice. Second, the frequencies of oscillatory eigenmodes of ferroelastic structural units correspond to the SubMM range of waves. Third, ferroelastic compounds are polymorphous, therefore they display extremely high sensitivity of their eigenmodes to small variations of temperature in the vicinity of polymorphic transformation. Due to these facts dielectric properties of such materials on a fixed frequency can vary over a wide range at the expense of controlled variation of temperature T in the vicinity of its critical value T/sub c/. The subject of the present work is the influence of polymorphism of ferroelastic solid-state structures on propagation of SubMM waves.

articleTitle: ESR spectra of chromium(V) complex under saturation conditions at low temperatures
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: As a consequence of the spectroscopic studies of the electron spin subsystem for the EHBACr/sup V/, EHBA(D)Cr/sup V/ and HMBACr/sup V/ complexes, the parameters of ESR spectra have been determined. The differences in a behavior of ESR line width depending on the microwave power have been revealed. The observable effects of the widening and narrowing of ESR lines for EHBACr/sup V/ and HMBACr/sup V/ complexes under microwave saturation conditions have been validated by the theoretical model based on averaging of a resonance magnetic field of molecules in all directions given that the molecules are oriented chaotically. It has been shown that one of the reasons in the visible difference of the behavior of ESR line width for the substances noted above is the different conformation of their molecules.

articleTitle: Ultra-stable Peltier-cooled low-noise 3-mm-wave-band receiver
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Such features as the highest sensitivity and stability are characteristic of SIS/HEMT cryogenically cooled receivers being used in radioastronomy, while the "conventional" superheterodyne receiver based on a Schottky-diode mixer and GaAs FET IF-amplifier, is preferred as a general-purpose device. This paper briefly describes a design technique for upgrading a "worn" (i.e. cryogenics-free) receiver from the radiometric standpoint: improvement in noise and stability performances. The specific device has been designed for the highly promising 3-mm band. The full-height waveguide whisker contacted mixer (DSB conversion loss no more than 2.1 dB over 85-115 GHz) and ultra-low-noise FET preamplifier (NF close to 0.5dB, operation band 1.2-1.7GHz) are similar to that described previously. An added reduction of the receiver noise temperature (DSB Tn is about 250 K) has come about through moderate (to -75/spl deg/C) cooling of the mixer/IF-amplifier only by a 3-stage semiconductor Peltier cooler. As far as could be determined from the literature, 250 K is the best value for non-cryogenic receivers in the appropriate frequency band.

articleTitle: Range of applications of a K/sub a/-band interferometric synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The present paper gives a detailed description of the concept, end-to-end design, and range of applications of a high resolution Ka-band interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR). The study is based on an existing system called AeS-1, which is working in X-band at 9.55 GHz and has been designed and manufactured by Aero-Sensing Radarsysteme GmbH, Germany. This radar system is configured as a two-antennae single-pass interferometric SAR with a ground resolution up to 0.5 m /spl times/ 0.5 m and a height accuracy up to 5 cm. It was first flown in August 1996 and has been in operational use since October 1996. In numerous flight campaigns, data covering several hundred thousands of km/sup 2/ have been acquired, processed to georectified digital elevation models and radiometrically calibrated SAR magnitude images, and finally post processed to value-added products like height, contour maps, topographic map sheets or city models.

articleTitle: Power orotron-type Ka-band amplifier
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The first results on experimental investigation of two-stage resonance generator and amplifier have been demonstrated recently. The electrodynamics system was composed of two identical stages formed by open resonator (OR) and lamella-type periodic structure (PS) situated on a plane mirror. The milling technology of PS had provided a period accuracy of the order of 5-6%. As we determined by modeling such period accuracy may be the origin of bad device efficiency and gain by reason of bad synchronism mechanism. In addition the inaccuracy of beam transfer channel height limited the beam current. To improve the PS period and channel accuracy up to 0.7% we modified the design and used the electrospark technology. The search of optimal gain and efficiency regimes by computer-aided design is covered.

articleTitle: Simultaneous ground based millimeter-wave soundings of stratospheric ozone in Apatity (67/spl deg/N, 35/spl deg/E) and Nizhny Novgorod (56/spl deg/N, 44/spl deg/E) during the winter 1999/2000
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The necessity of synchronous microwave observations of ozone behaviour on altitudes from 20 up to 60 km in polar and mid-latitude is caused by steady drop (in 90-ths of former century) its content in stratosphere of Northern Hemisphere. The largest declination of ozone happens on level about 19-20 km (potential temperature 465 K) in March in region covered latitude higher 60N. In this work the results of simultaneous microwave observations of stratospheric ozone in middle and polar latitude during the winter and spring 1999/2000 performed on SOLVE program are presented. The SAGE-III Ozone Loss and Validation Experiment (SOLVE) is a measurement campaign designed to examine the processes which control polar to mid-latitude stratospheric ozone levels.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic oscillations in a cavity with a nonlinear dielectric
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The thesis is devoted to problems of solving Maxwell's equations in the cavities containing nonlinear medium. The cylindrical cavity with a bounding surface of the complicated form is considered. With the purpose of obtaining a solution the method of evolutionary equations (or method of modal basis) is used. It allows one to investigate the cavities with time-varying or nonlinear mediums and without the limitations on the constitutive relations and on the functions of impressed sources, namely: to take into account all time-varying or nonlinear effects in mechanisms of polarization, magnetization and conductivity of a medium, that results in faithful representations for the unknown electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Gunn oscillator with barrel-shaped open resonator
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In the given work we embarked an attempt to modify a design of the barrel-shaped open resonator (BOR) with the aim to place and to match to it the semi-conductor generating elements (Gunn diodes). We have shown by experiment, BOR with a narrow rectangular groove can successful be used as a resonance system of solid-state oscillators. Power adders of several solid-state sources can be constructed on its basis.

articleTitle: Analysis of superconducting microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Telecommunication has certainly become, over the last years, one of the most promising fields of electrical engineering. In this context using patch devices in Terahertz range in this work, we will perform a photonic approach of a rectangular patch resonator over a double semiconductor substrate with superconductor material. This analysis will include a introduction of the TTL (Transverse Transmission Line) method, it's application to the resonator, and presentation of new results.

articleTitle: Resonances of microwave magnetic polaritons in iron borate
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The technique for investigation of magnetic polariton dispersion in antiferromagnetic crystals of iron borate is developed. For the first time, the volume polariton modes in free samples of FeBO/sub 3/ in static magnetic field H are observed and investigated at frequencies of 30-75 GHz. The nature of extra resonance lines of magnetic polaritons is discussed in the framework of size resonances.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave imaging of thin metallic wire by using interaction of it with dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The authors show that it is possible reconstruct an image of an object such as a metallic wire located in a dielectric waveguide after measurement of ratio P/P/sub 0/ (transmission coefficient) in accordance with the computer tomography scheme. The result of such image processing is presented. The aim of the work is to determine small conductivity inhomogeneities which are comparable with wavelength (3 mm) for different material. Thus, it will be possible to analyze about the quality of material in integrated millimeter wave technology.

articleTitle: Investigation of the detection, mixing and frequency multiplication in the planar semiconductor elements based on the high doped GaAs/AlAs superlattices in MM and SBMM wavelength bands
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Wide-miniband-superlattice devices are suitable for generation, detection,mixing and frequency multiplication of microwaves radiation. The devices, operated at room temperature, are based on nonlinear transport properties of the miniband electrons.

articleTitle: Aspects of generation of harmonic beams in non-relativistic free-electron lasers
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Presents the results of experimental and theoretical studies of electron beams moving along curvilinear nearly harmonic passes. A description of electrons in the Motz undulator is given for a case when there is a longitudinal external magnetic field. Under certain conditions of the ratio of the transversal and longitudinal field components the trajectories of electrons suffer substantial deformations, which lead to more complicated dynamics and, consequently, to the generation of higher harmonics of the cyclotron frequency.

articleTitle: The effect of atmosphere on the sea disturbed surface emission signature
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The calculation algorithms and computer programs for brightness effective temperatures of "underlying surface - atmosphere" system simulation are proposed in the millimeter wavelength range. The open grounds and disturbed sea surface are considered to be the underlying surfaces.

articleTitle: The radiometric survey time
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Possibility of passive detection of various objects in outer space, in the Earth's atmosphere, or on the Earth's surface has been demonstrated many times. However, useful results for passive detection may be obtained only by employing high-sensitivity receivers, scanning or multi-beam antennas of large area, effective survey algorithms, and statistical decision rules. The most important characteristics of a passive detection system are its range and survey time. The goal of this paper is to show the correlation between the parameters of a single-beam passive system for the observed object and the survey time. Minor factors are not taken into account in the paper.

articleTitle: Consequences of microwave irradiation on the different breeds of mulberry
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Numerous reports of microwave effects on biological objects are readily available. It is therefore indicated that one should study the nature of this process. The results of an investigation show that the mulberry in embryo is sensitive to electromagnetic radiation (EMR). Two breeds of the mulberry were subjected to low-intensity EMR-irradiation. The microwave EMR action during a period of 30 min was found to increase the caterpillar birth rate of both breeds by 5.8 percent and 13.6 percent respectively as against the scheduled figure. A caterpillar birth rate increase has been also obtained for the condition of SHF-irradiation over the course of 20 min. Close inspection of the data obtained shows that the trend and intensity of the silkworm edges (grane) reaction as a response to SHF- and EHF-action are a function of both the genotype (breed) and radiation dose (action time span). Typically, the weight of the male cocoon capsules varied directly to the irradiation time span, and the female cocoons lost weight after both EHF- and SHF-irradiation.

articleTitle: Application of atomic functions for construction of new classes of quadrature formulas
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Solving of many equations includes a phase of numerical integration using methods of Gaussian type quadrature. It was spread out using an approximation of the function with compact support (e.g. wavelet or atomic function). These functions are used in solving a different kind of problem e.g. for antenna synthesis, for solving a boundary value problem, for filter synthesis, for signal processing, and for image compression . Naturally it computed Gaussian quadrature with weight including the corresponding atomic function. Using these quadratures allows one to reduce computational costs, because one does not need to compute the value of atomic functions, and perhaps to increase the accuracy as compared with traditional Gaussian quadrature.

articleTitle: Possibility of mm-waves localization in quasi one-dimensional (quasi-periodic) system for the microwave resonant therapy
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this work, we propose, by numerical calculation, a possibility of mm-wave range localization to produce an irradiation of a bioobject at frequency f/spl ap/60 GHz (just near or at accupuncture points (AP) of human skin). Calculation shows that in one-dimension system/biosystem, a few hundred times intensification of the localized mm-wave range could be obtained. Such mechanisms have elsewhere been used to discuss the possibility of microwave localization to produce an experimental plasma fireball. Here we consider two types of one-dimensional disordered biosystems (AP), such as a quasi one dimensional (quasi-periodic) biosystem. and a fractal biosystem. A Fibonacci chain and a Cantor bar are chosen as a quasi-periodic biosystem and a fractal biosystem, respectively.

articleTitle: Integrated quasioptical millimeter wave multibeam antenna
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In the present article a modified beam-forming network (BFN) for quasioptical multibeam antennas is considered. We propose adding an array of coupled lines with fixed phase shifters to an array of insulated lines. The feed radiation pattern strives for a rectangular form due to these additional elements. As will be demonstrated, such a radiation pattern shape provides maximum optical system aperture efficiency without power spillage over its borders. At the same time the array period is rather small, to provide for the crossing of neighboring radiation patterns on the half-power level. One format for realizing BFN of multibeam antennas is based on a dielectric slotted waveguide (DSW) array. DSW has a low attenuation constant in comparison with the other transmission lines in millimeter waves.

articleTitle: MM wave sapphire quasi-optical resonator with conducting and superconducting endplates
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: This work is a result of studying the spectral and energy characteristics of sapphire quasi-optical dielectric resonator (QDR) with conducting endplates for purposes of small surface resistance R/sub s/ values measurement of high-T/sub c/ superconducting (HTS) film in the mm waveband. Basic theoretical relations for spectral and energetic characteristics of QDR, which made from sapphire single crystal with uniaxial anisotropy are given, experimental technique is briefly described and the first results of HTS film R/sub s/ measurement are given.

articleTitle: Synthesized pulse reflection by non-smooth surfaces in 8-mm wave range
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Composite dielectric structures are widely used as materials for solid-motor cases, thermal protection structures and sandwich radomes. Estimation of thickness and dielectric constant of every layer is very important for mechanical and radiophysical property prediction of the product. Microwaves provide non-contact measurements. The direct way to obtain reflection from the surface separately from other spurious reflections is to use time-domain reflectometry. For waveguide measurements it is more preferable to measure the reflection coefficient at a set of frequencies and transform experimental data from frequency to time domain using one of the spectral numerical algorithms. This approach is similar to time pulse probing. For plane surfaces, it was shown that the ratio of amplitudes of peaks for front interface of structure and metal plate was equal to Fresnel coefficient. The real machinery products of dielectrics have rough surfaces and cylindrical and spherical form. Many products of dielectrics have regular surface structure. Correct values of Fresnel reflection coefficient and the value of dielectric constant reconstructed are necessary for correct estimation of geometrical thickness of every layer. This situation induces some experimental problems in millimeter wave range scattering. The complexity of the situation is stipulated by properties of near-field radiation from real constructions of an open-ended waveguide.

articleTitle: On the calculation of the feeding coefficient of an open resonator of a diffraction radiation oscillator
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: For the oscillatory circuit, the diffraction radiation oscillator (DRO) uses a high-Q open resonator (OR), with electron-wave processes of the energy exchange proceeding on OR eigenoscillations. Given the wavelength and the OR geometry, wave types of the excitation can be both theoretically predicted and practically measured . The power transfer to the volume wave component of the OR oscillation comes about by virtue of the electron beam interaction with surface harmonics of the volume wave. When the resonator is open, the interaction gets more complex since a nonresonant noise associated with the electromagnetic energy radiation from the resonator is produced by an active power rather than reactive.

articleTitle: Optimization of the profiles of electrodynamic system of relativistic TWT by using atomic function
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The self-consistent two-dimensional nonlinear theory of a relativistic TWT with a slow-wave system in the form of an arbitrary irregular smooth waveguide, taking into account the average forces of the relativistic electrons interaction, is used. Equations of excitation are obtained by the method of transformation coordinates.

articleTitle: The use of mm-wave-dielectrometry for the cardio-vascular diseases early diagnostic, therapy and preventive maintenance
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Altered activity of the sympathetic nervous system is known to contribute to hypertension via neurohormonal stimulation of adrenergic receptors (ARs), which are members of the guanidine nucleotide superfamily and are divided into some major types. ARs are characterized according to their functional response to their stimulation or inhibition by various substances.Our investigation is devoted to the assessment of molecular mechanisms of transmembrane signal transduction into a cell by means of modeling of these processes under the condition of non-destructive control using the method of dielectrometry combined with traditional technology. The researches of dielectric characteristics in this millimeter wavelength allow to receive unique information about the water component of biosystems. The physical basis is the large difference between a dielectric permeability of biopolymers and bound water and a dielectric permeability of free water, because there is an area of free water dispersion in this range. This method is based on the analysis of conversions of the biopolymer-water matrix owing to conformational conversions of cell macromolecules at the binding of agonists, antagonists and modulators with membrane receptors.

articleTitle: Azimuthally periodic-corrugated cylindrical waveguide peniotron
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In the present work the mathematical model is offered and the program of account peniotron with electrodynamic system (EDS) as azimuthally periodic corrugation cylinder waveguide is developed. At construction of model the method of transformation of coordinates was used, at which there is a display of area of interaction to the regular cylinder and projective method of a finding of amplitudes of decomposition of the electrodynamic solution task of excitation on system of own functions unity radius cylindrical waveguide.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave and infrared electronics for investigations of acoustic-electromagnetic phenomena due to activity of Popocatepetl volcano
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The report is devoted to millimeter and sub millimeter electronics intended for research of acoustic-electromagnetic phenomena caused by Popocatepetl volcano (Mexico). The main purpose is to present different types of sensors, one of them is based on a red and infra red silicon detector (avalanche photodiode with separated regions of absorption and multiplication). This sensor guarantees both a good sensibility and a wide range of sensing in infra red range. It has the advantage of a realization as a planar array. For millimeter and sub millimeter radar measurements, using a modulator based on the surface oriented p-i-n structure with "deep" junctions is possible. For the remote measurements of basic meteorological parameters and chemical state by means of radio brightness temperatures (radiometer systems), a low noise receiver based on a dielectric waveguides and Schottky diodes cooled by means of cryoelectronic elements can be used.

articleTitle: A method of selective suppression of pattern sidelobes of linear arrays and continuous radiators
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Suppression of patterns sidelobes of antennas remains by an acute problem of antenna theory and engineering many years already. The special importance is given to this problem in radiometric systems, where receiving of the signals with low level is carried out, therefore in such systems rigid requirements are demanded to the suppression of interference signals. With development of adaptive arrays the accent was partly moved from a problem of general suppression of pattern sidelobes to a problem of their selective suppression. The present work is devoted to the given problem also.

articleTitle: Combined gyro-Cherenkov type of interaction of the wave HE/sub 11/ of a corrugated waveguide with an electron beam
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Research on the combined gyro-Cherenkov type interaction of a spiral electron beam with a rotating HE/sub 11/ wave of irregular corrugated circular waveguide was carried out. The results show that the creation of a highly effective TWT with an efficiency >60% is possible, thus leading to the extraction of both cross and longitudinal energy from the electron beam.

articleTitle: Resonance modes in the layered anisotropic dielectric rod resonators
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this work the analysis of spectral characteristics of an anisotropic radial-two-layer disk dielectric resonator (DDR) with ideally conducting planes of end walls was carried out. The obtained characteristic equation was numerically studied for an isotropic ring DDR. The frequency increase and Q-factor decrease of resonance oscillations was revealed with a decrease of dielectric layer thickness.

articleTitle: Optimization of wave-conversion on the cascade of thin round diaphragms
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Discusses more effective algorithms of the analysis of a wave diffraction on diaphragms in circular guides (extremely necessary for optimization applications requiring multiple recurrence of calculation of the characteristics of wave scattering). For the considered structures the situations of maximal conversion of the lowest symmetric wave in higher modes and concentrations of energy of conversion in a previous field are revealed.

articleTitle: Global optimization method for quasi-optics multiple diodes power combiner
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this paper we use quasi-optical techniques, millimeter techniques and a global optimization method techniques to design a higher fundamental mode power, larger fractional power of fundamental mode power and greater combining efficiency quasi-optical power combiner. The structure of the quasi-optical power combiner includes a spherical reflector, the radius of curvature of which is R and a hybrid reflector that is called the input reflector. The monolithic source-array is made up of 25 Gunn diodes that are mounted of parallel brass bars that have low thermal resistance. The bars are fixed on the inner plane surface of the hybrid reflector that is made up of a plane and a spherical surface with radius of curvature R.

articleTitle: The polarization and absorption character of the sequentially connection of the heterogeneities of the same type
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The common theory of the multilink waveguide and quasi-optical filters of the UHF range and millimeter waves has been developed in previous works. The technological inaccuracy, which is inevitable in practical devices, causes a serious change in the operational characteristics. In particularly, defects in the periodicity influence to a degree the band and resonant selection. The analysis of the influence of such defects on the device characteristics allows one to expand the functionalities of the multilink selective systems.

articleTitle: An analytical technique for calculating the surface impedance by using an approximate model of the current distribution in a superconducting thin film
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: In this paper, an approximate analytical method for calculating the surface impedance of superconducting thin film is presented. This method is based on Maxwell's equations, vector identities, Stoke's theorem, Gauss's theorem, differential operations in various coordinates and Poynting's theorem analysis for an approximate model of the current distribution in a superconductor thin film. The physical basis for the approximate analytical treatment leading to the calculation of the surface impedance is described. The mathematical details of the calculation is also given. The obtained results are presented in analytical and graphical form. The computer simulation results are verified by comparison with results using surface impedance formula of Mattis-Bardeen theory.

articleTitle: Optimization of the thermodynamic characteristics of bolometric film structures
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The main advances in the film technology of HTSC and manganite containing materials during the last ten years are related to different electrical properties. A few efforts were directed at the investigation of thermodynamics characteristics. As a result the best modem film structures are not optimal for bolometric application. This is clearly seen from the low operating speed of non-cooled manganite bolometers. To improve the characteristics of HTSC bolometers, hybrid constructions in the base of the film structure were designed. However, even in the case of room and higher temperature bolometers this problem can be resolved directly with the help of optimization of the thermal kinetic coefficients of the film structure. The quantitative analysis of this possibility is the purpose of the author's work.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field transformation caused by the plasma appearance in a flat waveguide
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The transformation of temporary and spatial electromagnetic field distribution caused by change in time domain of medium properties is investigated. The electromagnetic field in a flat waveguide with absolutely conducting plates is considered. It is assumed that until zero moment of time the waveguide was empty and electromagnetic field is excited by an axial symmetric current which has time dependence.

articleTitle: Heterodyne interferometer on the basis of the ring submillimeter laser with bidirectional optical pumping
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Laser submillimeter (SMM) interferometers are widely used to diagnose high-temperature plasma in thermonuclear installations. The results of a study of a ring SMM laser with bidirectional optical pumping in the formic acid molecule (HCOOH) acting by the oscillation line with the wavelength 393.6 /spl mu/m and heterodyne interferometer are given. The problem of stabilization of radiation sources in this interferometer is simplified substantially to increase reliability and reduce the cost of the interferometer.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave facilities at IRCTR, Delft University of Technology
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The International Research Centre for Telecommunications-transmission and Radar (IRCTR) as a research institute sees the challenge to be prepared to facilitate research in these new frequency ranges. For that reason, with help of the Dutch Technology Foundation STW, a sophisticated millimeter wave laboratory-has been realized and became operational mid 1999. Besides the installation of hardware facilities, a software environment for the development of high frequency components and systems also became operational.

articleTitle: Focusing laminar electron beams of high density with the trajectories of required configuration
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Formation of high density electron beams is complex due to the very strong Coulomb interaction in the tightly focused beam. Therefore, a magnetic field is normally required, in addition to a properly configured electric field, in order to compress a stream of accelerated particles into the dense beam. Unfortunately, the magnetic field essentially complicates the internal beam structure due to heavy mixing of the electron trajectories that may be unacceptable in some applications. In addition, it is a complicated problem to calculate both the electric and magnetic fields in any combined electromagnetic system producing high-density electron beams (Forrester, 1988; Szilagyi, 1988; Hawkes and Kasper, 1989). In order to overcome the complications, another approach was developed based on considering and solving numerically a series of more general well-posed boundary value problems instead of a single problem arising due to the conventional approach. According to Yurchenko (Microwave and Opt. Tech. Lett. no. 10, pp. 104-108, 1995), some functions used for imposing the boundary conditions could be chosen arbitrarily so that a series of solutions for the electric and magnetic fields is obtained. In general, any of these could be used as the final solution as they all yield a solution to the original problem providing the required spatial structure of the beam. In this paper, we apply this approach to a special case of a beam with rapidly converging electron trajectories when an analytical solution to the part of the problem can be found (Yurchenko and Yurchenko, 2001). We compute some configurations of the electric and magnetic fields needed to prepare the dense laminar electron beams with the required trajectories.

articleTitle: Simulation of adaptive two-parametric filtration of millimetric wave band signals
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: When using radiowaves in the millimetric range for radar-location and communication, researchers and developers of radio engineering systems are faced with the problem of non-stationary signals analysis. For their processing with a noise background, devices with parameters varied in time are used. Adaptive filters, which work based on a two-parametrical representation of random signals (TPR adaptive filters), are such a class of such devices. In this paper the authors present the simulation of adaptive two-parametric filtering of millimetric wave band signals.

articleTitle: The energy characteristics of the Gunn diodes on the basis of In/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As with blocking of the metal cathode contact
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: There are some ways of increasing the frequency limit of operation and efficiency of generation by Gunn diodes. There is a search for new semiconductor materials, which can be used as a material for transit electron devices (TED) and Gunn diodes in the resonant-transit mode, which allows them to achieve acceptable values of efficiency of generation at frequencies, some times exceeding the transit frequency. An important factor influencing the high-frequency limit of operation of Gunn diodes is the type of cathode contact, which appreciably determines the area initial heating of electron (AIHE) at the cathode. Previously the possibility of generation by Gunn diodes on the basis of In/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As material with a homogeneous structure of the active area of the diode and with high-resistance heterogeneity at the cathode has been investigated and the perspective use of this semiconductor material for Gunn diodes was shown. Also it has been shown that the perspective use of a metal cathode contact (especially for generation of frequency at the second harmonic), allows substantially reduced AIHE at the cathode and by that increases the efficiency of generation by the diodes. The purpose of the present work is to investigate the influence of the blocking metal cathode contact on the power and frequency characteristics of the Gunn diodes based on In/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As material.

articleTitle: Back-scattering from a chiral anisotropic conducting cylinder with a longitudinal slot
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The back-scattering of electromagnetic waves is investigated from a thin hollow anisotropic; conducting cylinder with a longitudinal slot. If the pitch angle of the helical conductive lines is equal to zero, then, for the H-polarized wave, the electrodynamic object under consideration turns into a metal cylinder with a longitudinal slot. The latter object is characterized by a resonance at low frequencies. Previously it has been shown that, under certain relations between the pitch angle of the conductive lines and the angular width of the slot, this resonance is selective with respect to the waves of different types of circular polarization. In the present paper, we investigate the radar back-scattering cross section as a function of frequency for various orientations of the slot and the electric-field vector of the incident wave. Analytical expressions are obtained that describe the low-frequency resonance. The measurement results are presented for the radar back-scattering cross section in the microwave band.

articleTitle: Propagation characteristics of surface acoustic waves induced by a high-Tc superconducting thin film
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The surface impedance concept of a high Tc superconducting thin film based on the Two-fluid model is used to study the propagation characteristics of a surface acoustic wave (SAW). In this study, the attenuation constant is depicted to discuss the effects due to frequency and temperature (mechanism of the losses). The slow wave propagation characteristics associated with the high temperature superconductivity (HTS) thin film technology make it possible to manufacture a compact-size circuit in microwave systems. The obtained results show that, low loss and negative part is occurred. As a results of low loss and hence negative part, the implementation of high gain amplifier becomes possible. The computer simulation results are verified by comparison with results using surface impedance formula of Mattis-Bardeen theory and show a good agreement.

articleTitle: Above plasma frequency radiation at intense beam-plasma interaction
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: For the case of large angle scattering beam the mechanism of plasma FEL brings to the spectrum broadening during beam-plasma interaction. This mechanism is mostly effective for the high-current beam because intensity of radiation is proportional to the squared density of the beam particles. If REB is not moment scattered then the beam-plasma instability itself leads to the excitation of broadband oscillation spectrum. For such values of the nonlinear dynamics the instability is chaotic. Excited oscillations are nonregular and have continuous spectrum. It should be noted that fast thermalization not only of plasma particles but the particles of the initially monoenergetic beam takes place. The above plasma frequency FEL-mechanism can make its contribution to the broadband spectrum excitation.

articleTitle: Fundamental microwave absorption in millimeter wave band in perfect dielectric crystals (physical basic and applications)
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: The technological progress that has been achieved in the interests of quantum electronics has made it possible to synthesize crystals of sapphire, ruby, and fluorite, as well as quartz, having extremely small numbers of structural defects. This makes it possible to investigate their dielectric losses in the millimeter wave band and to estimate the relative efficiency of the absorption mechanisms. The realization of this opportunity is interlinked, first of all, to research of an effective method of measuring extremely low dielectric losses in crystals in a millimeter wave band at low temperatures.

articleTitle: Empiric method for calculation electron beam cross-section pulsation in DRG
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Empirical method is proposed for determination of the static pulsation amplitude R of an electron beam (EB) in an electron gun in DRG and other microwave devices. Analytic formulas for R calculation are obtained for one version of the design of the ribbon EB gun. The results of theory are compared with an experiment.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of diffraction radiation on a metal-dielectric grating
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A rigorous method is advanced for solving excitation problems of Cerenkov and diffractional radiations by an electron flow driven near to a surface of metalodielectric diffraction strip grating.

articleTitle: Nonlinear multifrequency bunching in regular and irregular relativistic TWT
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Comparatively few works have been devoted to TWT with multifrequencies regime. Previous works about the multifrequency regime TWT have a great number of condition basing on mistake physical simplification. This article shows investigation of physical phenomenon of the nonlinear signals interaction, for example, the process of forming of electrons bunches, their shape and dynamic along the interaction area.

articleTitle: Stochastic properties of sphere cavity of millimeter wave band filled with randomly located sapphire particles
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: A new approach to experimental study of a problem of electromagnetic wave scattering on random inhomogeneities is proposed for study of quantum chaos effect in a quasi-optical electromagnetic microwave resonance system. In a Q-band the properties of a spectrum of natural oscillations in a spherical microwave cavity, filled by randomly located particles of a sapphire single crystal with reference sizes about the length of an electromagnetic wave in this material are investigated.

articleTitle: Reverse-biased GaAs- and Si-pnipn structures for semiconductor devices
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Research on the properties of reverse-biased pnipn structures with the aim of the creation of new semiconductor devices based on these structures is urgent. The present work is dedicated to this problem. As a mathematical model for the study of reverse-biased pnipn structures, the drift-diffusion model was used, which adequately describes the isothermal processes in semiconductors. The solution of the equations of this model is executed by the finite-difference methods for semiconductor structures with abrupt p-n junctions.

articleTitle: Efficiency and frequency band of the microwave GaAs-Gunn diode harmonic oscillators
publicationTitle: Fourth International Kharkov Symposium 'Physics and Engineering of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves'. Symposium Proceedings (Cat. No.01EX429)
abstract: Opportunities of expansion of band frequency tuning of oscillators on GaAs-Gunn diodes, operating in a continuous mode in a range of temperatures, represent doubtless interest for the developers high stability of the radioelectronic equipment of a microwave range. In this paper the dependence of band frequency tuning of harmonic oscillator MM-range of lengths of waves on GaAs-Gunn diodes from temperature of an environment is experimentally investigated.
